items.prompt: Given meeting time ranges, choose the largest number of meetings that don't overlap.
items.why: Interval scheduling: sort by end time and take every meeting that fits. The exchange argument makes the earliest finisher safe.

items.prompt: Coins come in arbitrary denominations (e.g. 1, 3, 4). Find the fewest coins that make an amount.
items.why: Greedy fails: 6 = 4+1+1 (3 coins) vs 3+3 (2 coins). Coins can be reused → unbounded knapsack DP.

items.prompt: nums[i] is your maximum jump length from index i. Can you reach the last index?
items.why: Keep the farthest reachable index while scanning; fail if i ever passes it. O(n), no DP table needed.

items.prompt: Items have weights and values; each can be taken at most once. Maximise the value within a weight limit.
items.why: Taking by best value/weight ratio fails when items can't be split. Choices interact → 0/1 knapsack DP.

items.prompt: Gas stations on a circular route have gas[i] and cost[i] to reach the next one. Find a start station from which you can complete the loop.
items.why: If total gas ≥ total cost a start exists. Whenever the running tank drops below 0, no start up to here works, so restart at the next station. One pass.

items.prompt: Given meeting intervals, find the minimum number of rooms needed so that no meetings clash.
items.why: Maximum concurrent overlap → sort by start and keep a min-heap of end times (or sweep start/end events). That's the Merge Intervals family.

items.prompt: Balloons are horizontal ranges; an arrow at x bursts all balloons covering x. Find the fewest arrows to burst them all.
items.why: Sort by end and shoot at the end of the first unburst balloon. Every balloon starting before that point is burst too, so it's interval scheduling in disguise.

items.prompt: Children stand in a line with ratings. Each gets at least one candy, and a child with a higher rating than a neighbour gets more than that neighbour. Minimise the total.
items.why: Two greedy passes: left to right for the left neighbour, right to left for the right neighbour, then take the max per child. O(n).
